name: mirador
tagline: An opinionated personal dashboard for your terminal
description: mirador is an opinionated personal dashboard for your terminal — world clocks, a calendar, weather, a real task list, notes, a market watchlist, live CPU and network charts, and more, laid out how you want them. It is built for one job: to sit in a terminal tab you leave open all day and glance at, so nothing blinks, nothing shimmers, and unfocused panels dim so exactly one thing is at full brightness. Thirteen panels include a full task manager with due dates and priorities, notes in a master-detail layout, an agenda read from a local .ics file, RSS headlines, a pomodoro timer, and a calculator with an adding-machine tape. Your data stays in plain TOML files you own — no database, no sync service, no account, and nothing phones home except the weather and market panels, which use free key-less endpoints. Layout is rearranged with m, themes preview with t, and every color is configurable.
highlights: Thirteen glanceable panels: clocks, calendar, weather, tasks, notes, markets, news, and more
Built to sit in a tab all day — nothing blinks, nothing nags, unfocused panels dim
Real task list with due dates, priorities, tags, and full editing
Plain TOML data files you can hand-edit, git, or delete — no account, no telemetry
Layout, themes, and colors fully configurable and rearranged from the keyboard
curatorNote: Most terminal dashboards are built to be watched; mirador is built to be glanced at. The product discipline — a status bar that names one thing and never counts, panels that dim instead of blink — makes it a genuinely thoughtful take on the genre, created July 25 and still under 300 stars.
